note: Every number below is copied from the module's own report files (ml_water/, ml_electricity/, ml_sectors/, ml_iot_demo/). Criteria were written down before training; each final test was run once, or never.

models.model: Model C: predictive residual (HistGradientBoostingRegressor), trained on normal operation only
models.data: BATADAL dataset03 (normal) / dataset04 (attacks 1-3 validation) / attacks 4-7 held out
models.why: Learns how the plant normally behaves and flags large prediction misses, so it can flag attacks with no signature. Used as advisory evidence only, on historical replay.

models.stage: Final test passed (as a screening signal)
models.model: Random Forest, 100 trees, load-invariant features, attack threshold 0.655
models.data: MSU-ORNL three-class release: data1-9 train, data10-12 validation, data13-15 held out
models.why: Right 95% of the time when it flags, but flags only about 40% of attacks. Approved as an investigate signal, never as a detector or an all-clear.

models.model: Random Forest on network + biometric features (data-alteration advisory)
models.why: The attack signature (extra network delay) is real and was caught every time. But the held-out period had more normal latency spikes than training (11.3% of normal flows against 3.2%), and the model read them as attacks: about 1 normal flow in 14 raised an alarm. Retuning after seeing the test would be fitting to the test, so it stays a negative result.

models.model: Best of LR / Random Forest / HistGradientBoosting: HGB
models.data: UNSW-NB15 research benchmark (lab traffic, not operator or 5G); 42% duplicate training rows handled by grouping
models.why: Strong headline numbers (ROC-AUC 0.993) hid a weakness: on attack records it had not effectively seen before, recall fell to 0.745, and it caught only 36% of fuzzing attacks.

models.model: Best of LR / Random Forest / HistGradientBoosting: HGB
models.data: Synthetic traffic-control simulator v2 (passed its own 8 shortcut audits); v1 rejected earlier

gates.name: False alarms during real detector faults

models.why: It could not tell attacks from ordinary sensor faults: during natural detector faults 11% of normal intervals raised an alarm, and it covered only 70% of harmful attack events.

models.stage: Not trained under the protocol; demonstration benchmark added
models.data: TON_IoT (one normal session) and CICIoT2023 curated derivative (no session fields; capture artefact 'Number')
models.final_test: protocol test impossible; demonstration test run once
models.why: The protocol needs splits grouped by capture session so a model is tested on traffic it has not seen. Neither dataset allows that. The demonstration below follows the audit's option 3 and is labelled as an in-distribution benchmark.
